text: The ETL job runs when you start it. COPY runs when you execute it. Every piece works, but that's not what Finance asked for back in Lesson 1 — they asked for numbers that update on their own, every night, without anyone remembering to kick off a job.

An EventBridge Scheduler rule, northfield-nightly-refresh, fires once a day on a cron schedule, five AM UTC, and its target is simple: start the Glue job northfield-orders-etl. That's the entry point for the whole chain.

Starting the ETL job isn't the finish line — the curated Parquet it produces still needs loading into Redshift. A Glue job trigger, northfield-load-trigger, watches northfield-orders-etl for a SUCCEEDED state, then starts a small Python Shell job, northfield-redshift-load, which re-issues the same COPY statement from Lesson 5.

That CONDITIONAL setting matters. A trigger that just fires on its own timer could start the Redshift load before the curated data has finished writing, loading stale or partial data. Watching specifically for SUCCEEDED means the load only ever starts once there's something correct sitting in the curated zone.

This deliberately isn't Step Functions — no branching, no built-in retries, no automated alerting. For a two-step chain, a schedule plus one conditional trigger is enough to remove the 'someone has to remember' problem. The Advanced tier picks up exactly that complexity later. Next: building the actual report Finance asked for, on top of this now-automatic pipeline.
